query: Which clinical factors best explain longer visit durations?

per_column.name: visit_type_category
per_column.rationale: A clean clinical taxonomy (wellness, acute illness, chronic followup, injury, emergency, procedure) that gives a strong grouping axis for explaining visit duration. Samples map soundly to source text (annual exam->wellness, viral URI->acute illness, MI followup->chronic followup, twist injury->acute injury). Well grounded and non-redundant with department/urgency.

per_column.name: condition_acuity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal acuity scale is a genuine explanatory axis distinct from urgency (which is administrative). Sample values are defensible readings (viral URI low, knee injury moderate). Some overlap with urgency but adds finer clinical severity gradation; groundedness reasonable.

per_column.name: procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure occurred is plausibly a strong duration driver, and near-constant 'no_procedure' still separates a meaningful minority. Sample rows correctly show no_procedure where text describes no procedure. Well grounded from text.

per_column.name: admission_or_urgent_referral
per_column.rationale: Disposition captures visit complexity/escalation, a reasonable duration correlate. Mostly grounded; the knee-injury row labeled 'routine_referral' is a mild inference (MRI ordered implies referral) but warranted. Dominant discharge_only leaves useful variance.

per_column.name: counseling_complexity
per_column.rationale: Counseling load plausibly drives duration and offers a distinct axis. However it is more inferential: 'moderate_counseling' is assigned as a default even to a MI followup that mostly says continue regimen, so some values are weakly supported by explicit text, lowering groundedness somewhat.

per_column.name: multimorbidity_signal
per_column.rationale: Reasonable axis for duration, but grounding is shaky: the annual-exam row (single mild fatigue finding) is labeled 'multiple_active_conditions', which the text does not support. Overlaps heavily with the near-duplicate multimorbidity_or_polypharmacy column.

per_column.name: multimorbidity_or_polypharmacy
per_column.rationale: Nearly a restatement of multimorbidity_signal with almost identical distribution and same category labels; adds little new analytical leverage. Individual sample values are better grounded here (annual exam -> single_condition), but redundancy strongly caps usefulness.

judge.rationale: Most added columns supply genuine clinical axes (visit type, acuity, procedure, disposition, counseling) that are relevant and non-trivial for explaining visit duration, and are largely derivable from the reason_for_visit text. Two weaknesses: the two multimorbidity columns are near-duplicates (one is essentially a restatement of the other), and multimorbidity_signal shows an unsupported 'multiple_active_conditions' label on a simple annual-exam row. Counseling_complexity trends toward a default 'moderate' value, weakening its groundedness. Overall the set is useful and mostly grounded, with localized hallucination and one redundant column.
